claims.proposition: U.S. data-center electricity demand is increasing materially and raises the need for generation and grid infrastructure.
U.S. generator interconnection queue throughput and study duration materially delay the addition of generation resources.
Large-power-transformer supply and multi-year lead times constrain the pace of transmission/substation expansion.
AMER data-center switchgear lead times are long enough to create a deployment timing bottleneck.
Eaton's completed Texas expansion more than doubled its U.S. production capacity of voltage regulators and three-phase transformers.
Eaton is investing in additional U.S. transformer production to address a critical transformer shortage and data-center/grid demand.
Eaton is adding U.S. medium-voltage switchgear manufacturing capacity in response to AI data-center demand and electrical supply-chain constraints.
GE Vernova is expanding U.S. switchgear and grid-equipment manufacturing capacity specifically to shorten lead times and connect energy-intensive loads including data centers.
Integrated onsite generation and modular electrical systems can provide a partial deployment-relief path for data centers facing grid-access delays.
Bring-your-own power and cooling infrastructure is being offered as a deployment-relief path in power-constrained U.S. data-center markets.
